newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries dip in London, nervous pre-Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries dip in London, nervous pre-Greenspan.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries lost ground in London on Monday, depressed by the weakness seen at the end of last week, and ahead of testimony from the U.S. Federal Reserve chairman next session, traders said.
"The market's been better offered all morning," said Charles Quigley, vice president at Chase in London. "We've seen better sellers out of the Far East in the two- to five-year sector."
The U.S. 30-year long bond was at 101-06, yielding 6.53 percent compared with 101-09 at the New York close. Tokyo markets were closed for a public holiday.
September T-bond futures were down 6/32 at 114-00 in automated trade.

On Tuesday Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan gives his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony. Traders and analysts said they expected to see some downside going into that, but moves were likely to be limited to a maximum of half a point.
Treasuries eased back from highs last week, both on concerns about U.S. interest rates, and also fears that the recent strong rally has left little room for another run higher.
From a technical perspective, Quigley said the market was not looking good, and more correction was suggested by the slow stochastics which were giving overbought sell signals.
But once Greenspan's statement is out of the way, the market could be set for another move upwards.

"There's a chance Greenspan is in the process of switching camps from the inflation pessimists to the inflation optimists," said Nigel Richardson, head of bond research at Yamaichi International in London. "If the testimony shows that then we'll see further upside."
Richardson said inflation appeared to be under control, leaving the Fed able to keep rates on hold for the time being.
"If there's no threat from inflation, you might see people's thinking moving from looking for a hike, to looking for the opposite," he said. "The balance could be perceived to be changing."
